hindi: अभिमन्त्रित करके मैं सिद्धि के लिए शव-शारिका को ग्रहण करता हूँ। जय हो, और जय होती है; शलक-भूतों को नमस्कार, स्वाहा।
english: Having consecrated [it], I take the corpse-śārikā for the sake of success. Let [it] conquer, and [it] conquers; homage to the śalaka-beings; svāhā.
notes: Obscure words rendered literally: śārikā (a bird, also a game-piece or small bone; here left untranslated) and śalaka-bhūta (śalaka = quill/splinter/porcupine; bhūta = being). The subject of jayatu/jayati is not stated. Unit 49 shows this verse is the mantra for the śava-śārikā.

words.gram: n. acc. sg. used as adv.
n. acc. sg. used as adv.

hindi: कुत्ते सुख से सोएँ, और जो गाँव में उत्सुक हैं। जिनके प्रयोजन सिद्ध हो गए हैं वे सुख से सोएँ, जिस प्रयोजन को हम खोजते हैं। जब तक उदय अस्त को प्राप्त हो, तब तक प्रयोजन और फल मेरा हो।
english: Let the dogs sleep happily, and those in the village who are curious. Let the siddha-arthas, whose aims are accomplished, sleep happily, [and] the object that we seek. Until the rising goes to setting, as long as [there is] the object, [let] the fruit [be] mine.
notes: Third line is obscure; rendered literally with the verb "be" supplied in brackets. The two clauses with yāvat are elliptical. siddhārtha also means white mustard seed; here rendered literally as "those whose aims are accomplished" (alternative: mustard seeds). kutūhala may also mean "noisy, restless".

hindi: इस प्रकार — स्वाहा।
english: Thus: svāhā.
notes: Closes the mantra of the preceding units; iti is rendered "thus".

hindi: इसका प्रयोग।
english: The application of this.

words.gloss: on the fourteenth of the dark half

hindi: चार भोजन का उपवास करने वाला कृष्ण पक्ष की चतुर्दशी को, भीड़ से रहित श्मशान में बलि देकर, इस मन्त्र से शव-शारिका को लेकर पौत्री-पोट्टलिका बाँधे।
english: Fasting for four meals, on the fourteenth of the dark half, in an uncrowded cremation ground, having made an offering and having taken the corpse-śārikā with this mantra, he should tie a pautrī-bundle.
notes: pautrī is obscure (not identified); rendered as a name, bundle = poṭṭalika. asaṅkīrṇa ādahane is resolved as asaṅkīrṇe ādahane (e before a vowel). Hyphen joins (kṛtvā-etena) are unsandhied in the e-text.

hindi: उसके बीच में साही के काँटे से बेधकर, जहाँ इस मन्त्र से गाड़ा जाता है, वहाँ वह सबको सुला देता है।
english: Having pierced it in the middle with the quill of a porcupine, wherever it is buried with this mantra, it puts all that to sleep.
notes: The object pierced and buried is not stated (presumably the bundle of unit 49). śvā-vidh = porcupine (lit. dog-piercer); śalyaka = quill. "tat sarvam" could also be "all there".

hindi: “मैं अग्नि, देवताओं और दसों दिशाओं की शरण में जाता हूँ; और सब दूर चले जाएँ; सदा मेरे वश में आ जाएँ।
english: “I go for refuge to Agni, the deities, the ten directions; and let all [things] go away; let [them] always come into my subjection.
notes: Opening quotation mark closes in unit 52. The neuter sarvāṇi has no stated referent. "apayāntu" (go away) sits oddly beside "come into my subjection"; the commentators may read otherwise (e.g. upayāntu "approach"), but the printed apayāntu is kept. śaraṇam is taken as acc. of the goal with upaimi ("go to for refuge").

english: Svāhā.”
notes: Closes the quotation opened in unit 51.

hindi: इसका प्रयोग।
english: The application of this.

words.gloss: one who has fasted three nights

hindi: तीन रात उपवास किए हुए, पुष्य में, इक्कीस बार सम्पात करके, शहद और घी से कंकड़ों पर आहुति दे।
english: Having fasted for three nights, under Puṣya, having made twenty-one pourings, he should offer upon the pebbles with honey and ghee.

text_flags.why: possible typo: extra ṣ; cf. upoṣitaḥ in units 64 and 79

notes: Printed uposṣitaḥ is a probable typo for upoṣitaḥ (cf. unit 64). "śarkarā" is śarkarāḥ with visarga dropped before e (pebbles, as in units 56-57); śarkarā can also mean sugar. puṣyeṇa is read as the lunar mansion Puṣya (the Sanskrit does not say "nakṣatra"). sampāta = pouring/dropping; the exact rite is not stated. The pebbles are the object of abhijuhuyāt (supplied from the context).

hindi: तब गन्ध और माला से पूजा करके गड़वाए।
english: Then, having worshipped [them] with perfume and garlands, he should have [them] buried.
notes: The objects (the pebbles of unit 54) are not stated.

hindi: दूसरे पुष्य में उठाकर एक कंकड़ को अभिमन्त्रित करके किवाड़ पर प्रहार करे।
english: Under the second Puṣya, having taken up one pebble [and] having consecrated it, he should strike the door.
notes: The printed token puṣyeṇa-uddhṛtya-ekāṃ is one token: puṣyeṇa, uddhṛtya, ekām. "Second Puṣya" = the next occurrence of the asterism; the object of uddhṛtya is not stated (the buried pebbles).

words.gram: n. acc. sg. used as adv.

hindi: भीतर, चार कंकड़ों का द्वार खोला जाता है।
english: Inside, of four pebbles, the door is opened.
notes: The printed abhyantarm is a typo (abhyantaram, or abhyantaraṃ). The syntax is obscure: the genitive "of four pebbles" may mean "by (the use of) four pebbles" or "as far as (the range of) four pebbles"; rendered literally.

words.gloss: on the fourteenth of the dark half

hindi: चार भोजन का उपवास करने वाला कृष्ण पक्ष की चतुर्दशी को टूटे हुए पुरुष की हड्डी से बैल बनवाए, और इससे अभिमन्त्रित करे।
english: Fasting for four meals, on the fourteenth of the dark half, he should have a bull made with the bone of a broken man, and should consecrate [it] with this.
notes: bhagna (broken) is left literal; it may mean a man with a broken limb or one broken/killed. etena "with this" refers to a mantra not given in the unit (presumably the preceding or following mantra). The token puruṣasya-asthnā is a hyphen join.

hindi: दो बैलों से जुती हुई बैलगाड़ी लाई जाती है।
english: A cattle-cart yoked with two cattle is brought.
notes: go-yāna is rendered literally as a vehicle drawn by cattle; āhṛtaṃ bhavati is "is brought/has been brought".

hindi: तब परम आकाश में रुक जाता है।
english: Then it stops in the highest sky.
notes: The subject is not stated (presumably the cart of unit 59). parama-ākāśa could also be "the supreme space". Obscure; rendered literally.

words.gloss: having the smell of the sun

hindi: सूर्य की गन्ध वाला, परिघमति, सबको भर देता है।
english: Having the smell of the sun, [it] parighamati, [it] fills everything.
notes: parighamati is not a known verb form (possibly from pari + √gham/√dham or a corruption); left untranslated. ravi-sagandha could be "of the same smell as the sun" or "with the smell of ravi (a plant name?)"; rendered literally. The subject is unstated. Obscure line.

words.gloss: flood of the essence of caṇḍālī, kumbhī, tumba and kaṭuka

hindi: “तू चण्डाली, कुम्भी, तुम्ब और कटुक के सार का प्रवाह है, स्त्री सहित भग है — स्वाहा।
english: “You are the flood of the essence of caṇḍālī, kumbhī, tumba [and] kaṭuka, the bhaga together with the woman — svāhā.
notes: Leading quotation mark in the print; it is not closed within this unit. The plant names (caṇḍālī, kumbhī, tumba, kaṭuka) are kept as names, not identified; caṇḍālī literally means an outcaste woman, kumbhī a pot, tumba a gourd, kaṭuka bitter. sāra-ogha = flood of essence, taken as a tat-puruṣa. sa-nārī-bhaga is obscure: bhaga may be fortune or the female organ; sa-nārī = with the woman. The printed dash token is kept as punctuation. Obscure line.

hindi: ताले खोलना और सुला देना।
english: Opening of locks and putting to sleep.
notes: A heading-like phrase naming the effects of the preceding rites.

words.gloss: one who has fasted three nights
of one killed by a weapon
of one impaled on a stake
danda with the editors doubt mark

hindi: तीन रात उपवास किए हुए, पुष्य में, शस्त्र से मारे गए या शूल पर बिंधे हुए पुरुष की खोपड़ी में, मिट्टी में, तुवरी बोकर, जल से सींचे।
english: Having fasted for three nights, under Puṣya, in the skull of a man killed by a weapon or impaled on a stake, in clay, having sown tuvarī, he should sprinkle [it] with water.

text_flags.why: possible typo: rāvāsya for rāvāpya (āvāpya, "having sown"); cf. unit 79 with āvāsya

notes: The printed tuvarī.rāvāsya-udakena is probably tuvarīr āvāpya udakena (tuvarīḥ + āvāpya), by comparison with unit 79 (guñjā āvāsya-udakena); the sya for pya is the likely slip, and the "." after tuvarī is a stray compound mark. tuvarī is kept as a plant name (not identified). The object sprinkled is not stated. The editors doubt mark (?) follows the final danda; the verse number 64 is printed inside the line.

hindi: उगे हुओं में से पुष्य में ही लेकर रस्सी बटे।
english: Of those that have grown, having taken [them] under Puṣya itself, he should twist a rope.
notes: The referent of jātānām is not stated (presumably the tuvarī of unit 64).

hindi: तब वह डोरी चढ़े धनुषों और यन्त्रों के आगे काटना, प्रत्यंचा को काटना, करता है।
english: Then [it] brings about, in front of strung bows and engines, a cutting, the cutting of the bowstring.
notes: The subject is the rope of unit 65. yantra is rendered "engines" (machines) literally.

hindi: जल-सर्प की थैली को स्त्री या पुरुष की उच्छ्वास-मिट्टी से भरे; नाक का बाँधना और मुख का जकड़ना।
english: He should fill a water-snake bag with breath-clay of a woman or a man; [the effect is] binding of the nose and seizing of the mouth.
notes: ucchvāsa-mṛttikā is obscure: literally "breath-clay"; it may be earth taken at a breath/death, or clay mixed with exhaled breath; "of a woman or a man" is taken with ucchvāsa. bhastrā = bag (skin bag, bellows). The words "[the effect is]" are supplied; the Sanskrit gives two bare nominatives. udaka-ahi is read as "water-snake".

hindi: सूअर की थैली को उच्छ्वास-मिट्टी से भरकर बन्दर की नस से बाँधे; आनाह का कारण।
english: Having filled a boar bag with breath-clay, he should bind [it] with monkey sinew; [this is] the cause of ānāha (obstruction).
notes: Printed ucchvāsamṛttikayā lacks the compound dot used in unit 67; split ucchvāsa-mṛttikayā. ānāha literally "binding up, tension"; rendered "obstruction", no diagnosis intended.

words.gloss: on the fourteenth of the dark half
of one killed by a weapon

hindi: कृष्ण पक्ष की चतुर्दशी को शस्त्र से मारी गई कपिला गाय के पित्त से राजवृक्ष की बनी शत्रु की प्रतिमा का अंजन करे; अन्धा करना।
english: On the fourteenth of the dark half, he should anoint an image of the enemy made of rāja-vṛkṣa wood with the bile of a tawny cow killed by a weapon; [this is] making blind.
notes: rāja-vṛkṣa (lit. king-tree) kept as a tree name, not identified. pitta is rendered "bile" in this non-medical context. "[this is]" supplied before andhī-karaṇam.

words.gloss: on the fourteenth of the dark half
of one impaled on a stake

hindi: चार भोजन का उपवास करने वाला कृष्ण पक्ष की चतुर्दशी को बलि देकर शूल पर बिंधे हुए पुरुष की हड्डी से कीलें बनवाए।
english: Fasting for four meals, on the fourteenth of the dark half, having made an offering, he should have pegs made with the bone of a man impaled on a stake.

hindi: इनमें से एक मल या मूत्र में गाड़ा जाने पर आनाह करता है; इसके पद या आसन में गाड़ा जाने पर शोष से मारता है; दुकान, खेत या घर में वृत्ति का उच्छेद करता है।
english: One of these, buried in dung or urine, causes ānāha; buried in his footprint or seat, it kills by wasting; in a shop, field or house it causes the cutting off of livelihood.
notes: Sandhi: nikhāta ānāham = nikhātaḥ ānāham (visarga dropped). ānāha kept as a term (literally binding up). eteṣām ekaḥ refers to the pegs of unit 70. The last clause names no act of burying; it is understood from the previous clauses.

hindi: इसी विधि से बिजली से जले वृक्ष की कीलों की व्याख्या की गई।
english: By this same procedure, the pegs of a tree burnt by lightning are explained.
notes: kīlakā vyākhyātāḥ = kīlakāḥ vyākhyātāḥ (visarga dropped).

words.gloss: with the cloth of a corpse

hindi: फिर, नया, नीचे की ओर, नीम, और जो काम-मधु है; बन्दर का रोम और मनुष्य की हड्डी मुर्दे के वस्त्र से बाँधकर।
english: Again, new, downward, nimba, and that which is kāma-madhu; monkey hair [and] a human bone, having bound [them] with the cloth of a corpse.
notes: Obscure: "punar navam avācīnam" is rendered word for word (punarnavā is also a drug name, but the tokens are printed separately); nimba is the name of a tree and kāma-madhu is obscure, both kept as names. The sentence continues in units 74 and 75-76.

hindi: जिसके घर में गाड़ा जाता है, या देखकर जिस स्थान पर वह ले जाए, वह पुत्र और पत्नी तथा धन सहित तीन पक्षों से आगे नहीं जाता।
english: In whose house it is buried, or, having seen [it], whatever place he may bring [it to] — he, with son and wife and wealth, does not pass beyond three fortnights.

text_flags.why: the dot is a stray compound mark; sadhanas + trīn is one phrase "with wealth, three"

notes: Line a is obscure: "yat padaṃ nayet" is taken literally ("whatever place/step he may bring [it] to"); the referent of "it" is the object of unit 73. In the printed sadhana.strīn the dot stands for the s+t sandhi of sadhanaḥ trīn. "Does not pass beyond three fortnights" = does not survive longer; literal.

hindi: फिर, नया, नीचे की ओर, नीम, और जो काम-मधु है; स्वयंगुप्ता, मनुष्य की हड्डी, जिसके पद में गाड़ी जाती है।
english: Again, new, downward, nimba, and that which is kāma-madhu; svayaṃguptā [and] a human bone — [he] in whose footprint it is buried.
notes: Obscure: "punar navam avācīnam" is rendered word for word (punarnavā is also a drug name, but the tokens are printed separately); nimba is the name of a tree and kāma-madhu is obscure, both kept as names. The sentence continues in units 74 and 75-76. svayaṃguptā (lit. self-guarded) may be a plant name; kept literal. pade is "in the footprint" as in unit 71. The predicate comes in unit 76.

hindi: घर, सेना, गाँव या नगर के द्वार पर, वह पुत्र और पत्नी तथा धन सहित तीन पक्षों से आगे नहीं जाता।
english: At the door of a house, an army, a village or a city, [it being buried], he with son and wife and wealth does not pass beyond three fortnights.

text_flags.why: the dot is a stray compound mark; sadhanas + trīn is one phrase "with wealth, three"

notes: The Sanskrit has no verb for the first line; "[it being buried]" is supplied from unit 75. See unit 74 on sadhana.strīn.

hindi: बकरे और बन्दर के रोम, बिल्ली और नेवले के, ब्राह्मणों के, श्वपाकों के, कौए और उल्लू के भी इकट्ठे करे। इससे कुचला हुआ मल तुरन्त उत्साद करने वाला होता है।
english: He should collect hairs of goat and monkey, of cat and mongoose, of brahmins, of dog-cookers, and of crow and owl. By this, crushed excrement is at once a cause of eradication (utsāda).
notes: The genitives in line b are taken with romāṇi of line a. avakṣuṇṇā is read as the participle of ava-√kṣud (to crush, pound); alternative "scattered". utsāda = rooting out, eradication; the object of the effect is not stated. Obscure last line. sadya utsāda = sadyaḥ utsāda (visarga dropped before u).

words.gloss: remains of a garland of the dead
skin of scorpion, āly(?), and snake

hindi: प्रेत की माला का अवशेष, किण्व, नेवले के रोम, और वृश्चिक, आल्य तथा सर्प की त्वचा — जिसके पद में गाड़ा जाता है, वह तुरन्त पुरुषत्व से रहित हो जाता है, जब तक वह हटाया नहीं जाता।
english: Remains of a garland of the dead, ferment, hairs of a mongoose, and the skin of a scorpion, āly(?) and a snake — he in whose footprint it is buried at once becomes without manhood, as long as it is not removed.
notes: The word āly(?) carries the editors doubt mark and is left untranslated. preta-nirmālikā is obscure (nirmālikā: remains of a garland); kiṇva = ferment (yeast). Plural subject items with a singular verb "buried" is as printed. apuruṣa is literal (without manhood; "impotent" would be an interpretation).

words.gloss: one who has fasted three nights
of one killed by a weapon
of one impaled on a stake

hindi: तीन रात उपवास किए हुए, पुष्य में, शस्त्र से मारे गए या शूल पर बिंधे हुए पुरुष की खोपड़ी में, मिट्टी में, गुञ्जा बोकर, जल से सींचे।
english: Having fasted for three nights, under Puṣya, in the skull of a man killed by a weapon or impaled on a stake, in clay, having sown guñjā, he should sprinkle [it] with water.

text_flags.why: possible typo: āvāsya for āvāpya ("having sown"); cf. unit 64

notes: Printed āvāsya is probably āvāpya (see unit 64, where the same slip occurs). guñjā = guñjāḥ (visarga dropped before ā). guñjā kept as a plant name.

hindi: उगे हुओं की अमावस्या या पूर्णिमा को, जब पुष्य का योग हो, गुञ्ज की लताएँ लिवाकर छोटे मण्डल बनवाए।
english: Of those that have grown, on the new-moon day or the full-moon day in conjunction with Puṣya, having had guñja vines taken, he should have small circles made.
notes: The referent of jātānām is the guñjā of unit 79. maṇḍalika "small circle/ring" is rendered literally; its use is not stated.

hindi: उनमें रखे हुए अन्न और पान के पात्र क्षीण नहीं होते।
english: Vessels of food and drink placed in those are not exhausted.
notes: "Those" = the maṇḍalika circles of unit 80.

hindi: रात्रि का प्रेक्षण आरम्भ होने पर, दीप की अग्नियों में, मरी हुई गाय के स्तन काटकर जलवाए।
english: When the night spectacle has begun, having cut out the teats of a dead cow, he should have [them] burnt in the lamp-fires.
notes: prekṣā = spectacle/show; rātri-prekṣā "night show" is rendered literally. pradīpa-agni could also be "lamp and fire"; taken as "lamp-fires".

words.gloss: with the urine of a bull

hindi: जलाए हुओं को बैल के मूत्र से पिसवाकर नए घड़े के भीतर लेप कराए।
english: Having had the burnt [teats] ground with the urine of a bull, he should have a new pot smeared inside.
notes: The printed antar.lepayet joins antaḥ and lepayet with a compound dot; split as two words. "[teats]" is supplied from unit 82.

hindi: उस गाँव की विपरीत दिशा में परिक्रमा कराकर, वहाँ जो इनका नवनीत रखा है, वह सब आ जाता है।
english: Having led [it] around that village in the reverse direction, whatever fresh butter of these has been placed there, all that comes.
notes: apasavya = to the left / anticlockwise, rendered "in the reverse direction". The object led around (the pot of unit 83) is not stated. "Of these" (eṣām) refers to the villagers, not stated.

words.gloss: on the fourteenth of the dark half

hindi: कृष्ण पक्ष की चतुर्दशी को, पुष्य के योग में, लगे हुए कुत्ते की योनि में काले लोहे की अँगूठी भेजे। गिरी हुई उसे स्वयं ले ले।
english: On the fourteenth of the dark half, in conjunction with Puṣya, he should send a ring of black iron into the womb of a dog that is "clinging"; he should take that [ring] when it has fallen by itself.
notes: lagnaka (lit. clinging, stuck) is left literal; it may mean a dog stuck together in mating. yoni kept as "womb". "svayaṃ patitām" = fallen by itself. The word "ring" in the second line is supplied from line a.

hindi: उससे बुलाए गए वृक्षों के फल आ जाते हैं।
english: By that, the fruits of trees, [when] summoned, come.
notes: "That" refers to the ring of unit 85. The input has no unit 86 (the numbering jumps from 85 to 87); no text is missing from the input itself.

hindi: मन्त्र और औषधि से युक्त जो गुप्त योग हैं और जो माया से रचे गए हैं, उनसे शत्रुओं का नाश करे और अपने जन की रक्षा करे।
english: The contrivances combined with mantras and remedies, and those made by illusion — with them he should destroy enemies and protect his own people.
notes: The printed samyuktā uses m for anusvāra; read saṃyuktāḥ. yoga rendered "contrivances" (cf. glossary, Book 12 sense). bhaiṣajya = remedies (no effect stated).
